en.title: Cost of Repeatedly Merging the Current Minimum and Maximum
en.description:
Each time, remove the current minimum and maximum elements of the array (they must be at two different positions) and insert their sum; the cost of this step is ceil((min+max)/(max−min+1)). Repeat until only one element remains, and find the total cost. Negative values are also rounded up in the mathematical sense.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric bounds are explicitly marked as site additions.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by n integers. The original has no numeric bounds; this site adds 1≤n≤200000, with elements in −1000000000..1000000000.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 8; -4; 0. These answers have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Store each element with a unique ID in both a min-heap and a max-heap, and use validity flags for lazy deletion. In each round, pop the two valid extremes, compute the exact ceiling, and insert the new element.
